definitions.full: H854. eth II. אֵת , preposition with — with makkeph אֶתֿ , with suffix אִתְּכֶם אִתְּךָ, אִתִּי, etc. (also, however, אוֺתוֺ אוֺתְךָ, , and similarly מֵאוֺתוֺ מֵאוֺתְךָ, etc.), first in Josh 10:25 ; 14:12 , next 2Sam 24:24 ; then repeatedly (but not exclusively) 1 Kings 20 — 2 Kings 8, & in Jeremiah, Ezekiel, e.g. 1Kin 20:25 (but 20:23 אִתָּם ) 22:7-8 , 24 (beside מֵאִתִּי ) 2Kin 1:15 ; 3:11-12 , 26 ; 6:16 (beside מֵאִתּוֺ ) 8:8 ; Jer 2:35 ; 10:5 ; 16:8 ; 19:10 ; 20:11 ; Ezek 2:6 ; 10:17 ; 23:23 ; 37:26 (see below 1d ; also Isa 59:21 , contr. Gen 17:4 : on אֹתָהּ שָׁכַב 34:2 and elsewhere, see below שָׁכַב , & compare Dr Sm ii. 13, 14 ) preposition denoting proximity (synonym עִם ; Phoenician את , e.g. CIS i. 3, 8 רפאם את משכב לם יכן לא let there not be for them a resting-place with the shades; Assyrian itti (perhaps akin to ittu 'side,' Dl Pr 115 Hpt KAT 2. 498 ; but compare Nö ZMG '86, 738 f. ). Not found as yet in the other cognate languages: but compare Ethiopic ' enta , towards, which supports the view; that אֵת is for ' int [compare תִּתִּי תֵּת, ], perhaps from √ אנה to meet Ol p. 431 Prät ZMG '73, 643 Lag M i. 226 ). 1 Of companionship, together with: Gen 6:13 behold, I destroy them אֶתהָֿאָרֶץ together with the earth, 11:31 ; 12:4 +? verbs of dwelling, abiding, going, etc., as Judg 1:3 ; 14:11 ; 19:4 , & in the phrase אִתּוֺ אֲשֶׁר הָעָם 4:13 ; 7:1 ; 9:33 , 48 ; 1Sam 14:20 ; 30:4 etc.; thou, and thy sons ֗֗֗ ׃ אִתָּֽךְ with thee Gen 6:18 ; similarly (3rd person) 7:7 , 13 ; 8:18 ; 9:8 and elsewhere (character of P: Dr Intr 124 ); אֶתהָֿאֱלֹהִים הִתְהַלֵּךְ to walk with God, i.e. to have him as a companion (that is, by adopting a course of life pleasing to him) 5:22 , 24 ; 6:9 (compare אֵת הִתְהַלֵּךְ literal 1Sam 25:15 ); — by the side of, like Isa 45:9 , equally with Lev 26:39 , in common with Jer 23:28 b (compare עִם 1e, f ). Hence, in particular — a. with for the purpose of help: Num 14:9 ׳וי אִתָּנוּ , Josh 14:12 ( אוֺתִי , as Jer 20:11 ) Judg 1:19 ; 2Kin 6:16 ; 9:32 מִי אִתִּי מִי who is on my side , who ? אֲנִי אִתְּךָ כִּי Isa 43:5 ; Jer 1:18-19 , +; Isa 63:3 ; Psa 12:5 our lips are with us, on our side ; in the phrase מּ יַד ׳(הָֽיְתָה) אֵת 2Sam 14:19 ; 2Kin 15:19 ; Jer 26:24 ; אֵת נָשָׂא to bear together with , i.e. to assist Exod 18:22 ; Num 11:17 . Exceptionally, = with the help of: Gen 4:1 for I have gotten a man ׳אֶתיֿ with the help of ׳י (compare עם 1Sam 14:45 ) Gen 49:25 (where, however, the parallelism, & ⅏ ᵑ6 ᵑ7 favour שַׁדַּי וְאֵל for שַׁדַּי וְאֵת ) Micah 3:8 ; compare Est 9:29 . b. beside (German neben ): Gen 39:6 מְאוּמָה אִתּוֺ יָדַע לֹא he knew not with him, beside him, aught (i.e. Joseph managed everything), 39:8 ; Exod 20:23 אִתִּ֑י תַעֲשׂוּן לֹא ye shall not make (aught) beside me. c. beside = in the presence of (rare): Gen 20:16 b and before all thou shalt be righted, Isa 30:8 ; Micah 6:1 . In this sense מּ ׳אֶתמְּֿנֵי is more frequently, see below מָּנִים d. of intercourse of different kinds with another, e.g. after verbs of making a covenant or contract, or (less often) of speaking or dealing: ( α ) Gen 9:9 ; 15:18 ; 17:4 ( Ezek 16:60 ; Isa 59:21 - אוֺת ) Josh 10:4 ; 1Kin 3:1 etc.; compare 1Sam 2:13 (but here מֵאֶתֿ הַכֹּהֵן is probably to be read with ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ᵐ5 Ke We etc., compare Deut 18:3 ). ( β ) Gen 17:3 ; 42:30 קָשׁוֺת אִתָּנוּ דִּבֶּר , 1Kin 8:15 ; Psa 109:2 , & especially in Jeremiah and Ezekiel (as Jer 1:16 ; 4:12 [ 52:9 אִתּוֺ ] 5:5 ; 12:1 ; Ezek 2:1 ; 3:22 , 24 , 27 ; 14:4 ; 44:5 — all - אוֺת ); Gen 24:49 to perform kindness אֵת ( עִם is here more Genl.), 2Sam 16:17 אֶתרֵֿעֶךָ֑ חַסְדְּךָ זֶה , Ruth 2:20 ; Zech 7:9 ; Jon 11:27 רָעָה אִתִּי עשֶֹׁה וְאַתָּה , Deut 1:30 ; 10:21 ; 1Sam 12:7 b, (- אוֺת ) Jer 21:2 ; 33:9 ; Ezek 7:27 ; 16:59 ; 22:14 ; 23:25 , 29 ; 39:24 ; absolute 17:17 ; 20:44 ; Psa 109:21 ; Zeph 3:19 ; ( γ ) in a pregnant sense, (in dealing) with , i.e. towards (rare): Isa 66:14 ; Psa 67:2 אִתָּנוּ מָּנָיו יָאֵר make his face to shine with (= toward) us (varied from אֶל Num 6:25 ) Deut 28:8 ; faithful with Psa 78:8 (compare 78:37 עִם נָכוֺן ); Ezek 2:6 ( אוֺתָ֑ךְ ); Judg 16:15 אִתִּי אֵין וְלֹבְּךָ . ( δ ) often with verbs of fighting, striving, contending, as Gen 14:2 , 8 , 9 ; Num 20:13 ; Isa 45:9 ; a 50:8 ; Psa 35:1 ; Prov 23:11 ; with בְמִשְׁמָּט בָּא Psa 143:2 ( Isa 3:14 and elsewhere עִם ). 2 Of localities, especially in the phrase אֵת אֲשֶׁר describing a site: Judg 3:19 ; 4:11 אֶתקֶֿדֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר which is near Kedesh, 1Kin 9:26 ; 2Kin 9:27 (compare עם 2 , which is commoner in this sense); Ezek 43:8 ; Exod 33:21 אִתִּי מָקוֺם הִנֵּה . Perhaps, anomalously, 1Sam 7:16 at or by all those places (but see Dr); in 2Sam 15:23 אֵת אֶתהַֿמִּדְבָּר, דֶרֶךְ עַלמְּֿנֵי = towards is against analogue: read with ᵐ5 L בַּמִּדְבָּר אֲשֶׁר הַזַּיִת דֶּרֶךְ עַלמָּֿנָיו ; 1Kin 9:25 אִתּוֺ beside it (that is, the altar); but עָלָיו 13:1 etc. would be idiomatic, & for אֲשֶׁר אִתּוֺ Klo proposes plausibly אֶתאִֿשֹּׁוֺ (see Exod 30:20 ). 3 מּ ׳אֵת denotes specially, a. in one's possession or keeping: Gen 27:15 ; 30:29 thou knowest ֗֗֗ אִתִּי מִקְנְךָ הָיָה אֲשֶׁר אֵת how thy cattle fared with me, 30:33 ; Leviticus 5:23; Lev 19:13 ; Deut 15:3 ; Judg 17:2 ; 1Sam 9:7 אִתָּנוּ מָה = what have we ? 25:29 ; Isa 49:4 my right is with Jehovah (contr. 40:27 ), Jer 8:8 ; Psa 38:11 the light of mine eyes also אִתִּי אֵין i.e. is gone from me, Prov 3:28 ; 8:18 ; in his power, Jer 10:5 אוֺתָם אֵין הֵיטֵיב is not in their power , perhaps Psa 12:5 . A dream, or the word of ׳י , is said to be אֵת with a prophet, 2Kin 3:12 ; Jer 23:28 ; 27:18 . Metaph. of a mental quality, Prov 11:2 ; 13:10 . b. in one's knowledge or memory: Isa 59:12 אִתָּנוּ מְּשָׁעֵינוּ our transgressions are with us , i.e. present to our minds (|| יְדַעֲנוּם וַעֲוֺנֹתֵינוּ ), Job 12:3 כְּמוֺאֵֿלָּה אֶתמִֿיאֵֿין with whom are not (i.e. who knoweth not ? τίς οὐ σύνοιδε ;) things like these ? 14:5 אִתָּךְ i.e. known to thee, Prov 2:1 ; Gen 40:14 ; Jer 12:3 (Ew Gf towards thee, as 1d γ ). So אֶתנַֿפְשְׁכֶם אִםיֵֿשׁ Gen 23:8 [ 2Kin 9:15 ׳נ alone], אֶתלְֿבָבְךָ 10:15 . compare עם 4b , which is more frequent in this sense. 4 מֵאֵת ( מֵאִתִּי , etc.; also - מֵאוֺת ) from proximity with (like Greek παρά with a Genitive, From de chez ; in Syriac, Arabic , corresponding synonym מֵעִם ; see below): coupled almost always with persons (contrast מֵעִם , a ). Thus a. with קָנָה to buy Gen 25:10 + often (compare 17:27 ); לָקַח 42:24 ; Exod 25:2 ; Lev 25:36 ; Numbers 17:17 + often; נָשָׂא Psa 24:5 ; שִׁלַּח , as Gen 8:8 מֵאִתּוֺ אֶתהַֿיּוֺנָה וַיְשַׁלַּח and he sent forth the dove from with him 26:27 ; הָלַךְ 26:31 ; 1Kin 18:12 ; 20:36 ; Jer 9:1 , of a wife deserting her husband Judg 19:2 מֵאִתּוֺ וַתֵּלֶךְ , Jer 3:1 (compare Isa 57:8 ); with simile words Gen 38:1 ; Deut 2:8 ; 1Kin 11:23 ; Jer 2:37 (see Exod 5:20 ); Isa 54:10 ; Psa 66:20 ; with שָׁאַל Judg 1:14 ; 1Kin 2:16 ; Psa 27:4 +, דָּרַשׁ 1Kin 22:7 and elsewhere, שָׁמַע 1Sam 2:23 . — מּ מְּנֵי ׳מֵאֵת Gen 27:30 ; 43:34 ; Exod 10:11 ; Job 2:7 ; Lev 10:4 ( הַקֹּדֶשׁ ), 2Kin 16:14 ( הַבַּיִת ). Hence b. of rights or dues, handed over from , given on the part of , any one: Gen 47:22 מַּרְעֹה מֵאֵת חֹק ; often in P, as 23:20 ; Exod 27:21 a perpetual due יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּנֵי מֵאֵת from , or on the part of , the children of Israel, Lev 7:34 ; b 24:8 ; Num 3:9 ; 7:84 +; Deut 18:3 ; 1Sam 2:13 ( ᵐ5 , etc.; see 1d ) 2Sam 15:3 הַמֶּלֶךְ מֵאֵת אֵיןלְֿךָ וְשֹׁמֵעַ but there is none to hear thee deputed of the king, 1Kin 5:14 . c. expressing origination: 1Kin 1:27 נִהְיָה הַמֶּלֶךְ אֲדֹנִי מֵאֵת אִם . Especially י ׳מֵאֵת — of a concrete object proceeding from him: Gen 19:24 (brimstone), Num 11:31 (a wind), 16:35 (fire), 1Sam 16:14 (evil spirit), Isa 38:7 (a sign), Jer 51:53 (wasters), Micah 5:6 (dew); of wrath Zech 7:12 (compare Num 17:11 ), teaching Isa 51:4 , the word of prophecy Jer 7:1 (so 11:1 ; 18:1 +? Jeremiah) 37:17 ; Ezek 33:30 ; with 'have I((we) heard' Isa 21:10 ; 28:22 ; Jer 49:14 (= Obadiah); of an event, or phase of history Josh 11:20 י ׳מֵאֵת הָֽיְתָה it came of ׳י to..., 1Kin 12:24 ; Hab 2:13 ; Psa 118:23 י ׳מֵאֵת זאֹת הָֽיְתָה ( ᵐ5 παρὰ Κυρίου ) Ezra 9:8 ; Neh 6:16 ; of trouble ( רָעָה ) 2Kin 6:33 ; Micah 1:12 ( יָרַד ); of a good or evil lot, having its source in ׳י Jer 13:25 ; Isa 54:17 ; Psa 109:20 , compare Job 2:10 ; Psa 22:26 תְהִלָּתִי מֵאִתְּךָ from thee cometh my praise (thou art the source of it); Isa 44:24 Qr מֵאִתִּי of myself (compare ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ John 5:30 ; Kt is אִתִּי מִי who was with me ?), John 54:15 מֵאוֺתִי אֶפֶס not at my instance (compare מִנִּי לֹא John 30:1, מִמֶּנִּי לֹא Hosea 8:4 ). d. of a place 1Kin 6:33 (corrupt: read with ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵐ5 [partly] רְבֻעוֺת מְזוּזֹת , & compare Ezek 41:21 ).Note. אֵת expresses closer association than עִם : hence while מֵעִם sometimes denotes hardly more than from the surroundings or belongings of , מֵאֵת expresses from close proximity to . Thus Saul asks, מֵעִמָּנוּ הָלַךְ מִי who has gone from (those) about us ? but Jacob, speaking of the loss of Joseph, says, Gen 44:28 מֵאִתִּי הָאֶחָד וַיֵּצֵא and the one is gone from with me. מֵאֵת is accordingly preferred to מֵעִם in the sense of origination or authorship; מאת is not usual in the sense of מֵעִם c , nor מֵעִם in the sense of מֵאֵת b. .
